jerseys.jersey-01:
Josh Dickinson was one of MoDo’s alternate captains in 2023/24, the club’s first season back in the SHL. The Canadian centre played all 52 regular-season games, recording 16 goals and 16 assists for 32 points.

MoDo secured its place in the top division for another season. Dickinson left the club at the end of the campaign. According to the collection’s dating, this jersey is from his final MoDo season, following his part in the team’s promotion to the SHL in spring 2023.
jerseys.jersey-02:
Lars Jansson played 50 regular-season games for MoDo in 1996/97, recording 11 goals and 8 assists for 19 points. It was one of his highest-scoring seasons in terms of goals for the club.

The defenceman became a long-serving member of MoDo’s defence. When a knee injury ended his career in 2005, he had played 15 seasons for the club and scored 86 goals, according to contemporary reporting by Sveriges Radio. This jersey represents his time at MoDo in the second half of the 1990s.
jerseys.jersey-03:
Markus Näslund returned to MoDo during the 2004/05 NHL lockout. He recorded 8 goals and 9 assists in 13 regular-season games, totalling 17 points at an average of 1.31 points per game.

The season brought several of the club’s biggest names back to Örnsköldsvik, including Peter Forsberg and brothers Daniel and Henrik Sedin. MoDo’s campaign ended in the quarter-finals. This jersey is associated with Näslund’s temporary return to Swedish club hockey during his established NHL career.
jerseys.jersey-04:
Mattias Weinhandl led MoDo in scoring in 2000/01 with 32 points in 48 regular-season games, evenly split between 16 goals and 16 assists. It was his second season with the club after joining from Troja-Ljungby.

MoDo had reached the Swedish championship final the previous year and would do so again in 2002. This season therefore fell between two appearances in the final during Weinhandl’s first spell at the club. After the 2001/02 season, he moved to the New York Islanders and hockey in North America.
jerseys.jersey-05:
Mattias Weinhandl returned to MoDo during the 2004/05 NHL lockout. He played all 50 regular-season games, scoring 26 goals and adding 20 assists. His 46 points made him the team’s leading scorer, ahead of players including Peter Forsberg and Henrik Sedin.

It was Weinhandl’s fourth season with MoDo’s senior team, following his first three years before joining the New York Islanders. This jersey is from a season when returning players gave Elitserien an unusually strong international presence.
jerseys.jersey-06:
Mattias Weinhandl recorded 16 goals and 16 assists in 48 regular-season games in 2000/01, leading MoDo in scoring. He had joined the club the previous year and won his first Swedish championship silver medal in spring 2000.

His first spell at MoDo lasted three seasons and brought another silver medal in 2002. He then continued his career with the New York Islanders. This jersey is associated with the period when Weinhandl established himself as an Elitserien goalscorer, before his NHL years and later return during the lockout.
jerseys.jersey-07:
Michael Hjälm recorded 37 points in 36 regular-season games for MoDo in 1982/83, with 13 goals and 24 assists. The young forward was already averaging more than a point per game early in his senior career.

It was the beginning of a career that included several spells at the club. MoDo’s own captaincy records list him as captain from 1988 to 1991. This jersey is dated to his early years, before he later took on the team’s formal leadership role.
jerseys.jersey-08:
Michal Zajkowski shared MoDo’s goaltending duties with Karol Křížán in 2005/06. Zajkowski appeared in 7 regular-season games and allowed an average of 2.78 goals per 60 minutes, according to the Swedish Ice Hockey Association’s statistics.

Coached by Harald Lückner, MoDo finished sixth in the regular season. This was the season before the club’s Swedish championship win in 2007. The jersey therefore represents the goaltending side of the team being built in the years before its second championship.
jerseys.jersey-09:
The collection associates this jersey with Niklas Sundström’s 2007/08 preseason. The previous spring, he had helped MoDo win its first Swedish championship in 28 years, having returned from the NHL ahead of 2006/07.

In the 2007/08 regular season, Sundström recorded 7 goals and 30 assists in 45 games for 37 points. His many assists underline his importance to the team’s attack after the championship season. The exact preseason use of this particular jersey remains to be confirmed.
jerseys.jersey-10:
Per “Pelle” Lundqvist recorded 16 goals and 10 assists in 36 regular-season games for MoDo in 1979/80. The season immediately followed the club’s first Swedish championship in 1979, when Lundqvist was part of the winning team.

He also represented Sweden at the 1980 Olympics, recording 4 goals and 3 assists in 7 games. The jersey is therefore dated to a season in which he combined his role as an established MoDo forward with playing on the Olympic stage.
jerseys.jersey-11:
Peter “Foppa” Forsberg was one of MoDo’s leading players as the club reached the Swedish championship final in 1993/94. He recorded 18 goals and 26 assists in 39 regular-season games for 44 points. Another 16 points in 11 playoff games followed, although Malmö won the final series.

That same winter, Forsberg won Olympic gold with Sweden in Lillehammer. It was his last full season in Swedish club hockey before his NHL debut in 1995. The jersey is associated with a year when he was already among Swedish hockey’s leading players, even before his North American career had begun.
jerseys.jersey-12:
Peter “Foppa” Forsberg returned to MoDo in 2009/10 after many years in the NHL and recurring injury problems. He recorded 11 goals and 19 assists in 23 regular-season games for 30 points, averaging 1.30 points per game.

It was his final season with MoDo’s senior team. A brief NHL comeback with Colorado followed in 2011 before his playing career ended. This jersey is therefore associated with the closing stages of his career and his last extended return to his hometown club.
jerseys.jersey-13:
Peter “Foppa” Forsberg firmly established himself in MoDo’s senior team in 1990/91. He recorded 7 goals and 10 assists in 23 Elitserien games. Alongside this, he produced 102 points in 39 junior games, with 38 goals and 64 assists.

In summer 1991, the Philadelphia Flyers selected him sixth overall in the NHL draft. The jersey is associated with his breakthrough season, when he combined junior hockey with playing at Sweden’s highest level, several seasons before his NHL debut.
jerseys.jersey-14:
Peter “Foppa” Forsberg returned to MoDo when the NHL season was cancelled during the 2004/05 lockout. In 33 regular-season games, he recorded 13 goals and 26 assists for 39 points, placing him second in MoDo’s scoring behind Mattias Weinhandl.

For Örnsköldsvik, it was an opportunity to see several of the club’s NHL stars together again. His teammates included Markus Näslund, Daniel Sedin and Henrik Sedin. MoDo reached the playoffs but lost to Färjestad in the quarter-finals.
jerseys.jersey-15:
In 2009/10, Peter “Foppa” Forsberg combined his return to MoDo with representing Sweden at the Vancouver Olympics. It was his fourth Olympic tournament, following Lillehammer in 1994, Nagano in 1998 and Turin in 2006.

In MoDo’s regular season, he recorded 30 points in 23 games: 11 goals and 19 assists. The jersey is from the later part of his playing career, when he was still producing more than a point per game in Swedish club hockey. Sweden finished fifth in the Olympic tournament.
jerseys.jersey-16:
Peter Holmqvist’s MoDo jersey is from the 1977/78 season. MoDo’s own historical records list a save percentage of 87.30% for him in the regular season.

He was part of the club’s goaltending lineup in the 1970s alongside Sune Ödling. A contemporary match programme from November 1974 confirms his place in the senior team.
jerseys.jersey-17:
Sune Ödling was one of MoDo’s goaltenders around the time Elitserien began. In the 1975/76 regular season, he appeared in 21 games and recorded a save percentage of 87.9%.

He later helped MoDo win its first Swedish championship in 1979 and also won World Championship bronze with Sweden that spring. The collection dates the jersey to 1974–1976, a few years before the championship success. Whether this jersey was used during one or more of those seasons remains to be confirmed.
jerseys.jersey-18:
Tobias Enström played 47 regular-season games for MoDo in 2005/06, recording 4 goals and 7 assists. He added another assist in 4 playoff games.

His development continued the following year, when he recorded 28 regular-season points and helped win the Swedish championship in 2007. He then began his NHL career with the Atlanta Thrashers. The jersey is dated to the season before the championship, placing it shortly before both the title and his move to North America.
jerseys.jersey-19:
Tomas Nänzen was MoDo’s captain during the 1993/94 season, when the team reached the final, according to the club’s own captaincy records. He recorded 5 goals and 6 assists in 39 regular-season games and also appeared in the team’s 11 playoff games.

MoDo reached its first Swedish championship final since winning the title in 1979, but Malmö became champions. The collection’s image filenames specify autumn 1993/94. The jersey is therefore associated with his season as captain, without any established use in the later final series.
jerseys.jersey-20:
This MoDo jersey is from Tommy Salo’s 2004/05 Elitserien season, after his NHL years. He appeared in 36 regular-season games, recording a save percentage of 90.9% and allowing 2.58 goals per 60 minutes.

This was the season when the NHL lockout brought several star players back to MoDo.
jerseys.jersey-21:
Tommy Själin was part of MoDo’s attack in the mid-1970s. In Elitserien’s first season, 1975/76, he recorded 10 goals and 6 assists in 28 regular-season games for 16 points.

A few years later, he helped MoDo win its first Swedish championship in 1979. The collection dates the jersey to 1974–1976, placing it early in his MoDo career. The exact season still needs to be confirmed before the jersey can be dated more precisely.
jerseys.jersey-22:
Tommy Själin recorded 22 goals and 21 assists in 34 regular-season games in 1983/84. His 43 points were just one fewer than scoring leader Dan Labraaten’s 44. Teammate Michael Hjälm also finished with 43 points.

Despite these strong individual performances, MoDo were relegated from Elitserien after the qualification round. Själin continued to produce in that round, recording 6 goals and 5 assists in 5 games. The jersey is associated with a season when his goalscoring contrasted sharply with the team’s results.
jerseys.jersey-23:
Ulf “Lillis” Hansson played for MoDo in 1979/80, the season after the club’s first Swedish championship. He recorded 3 goals and 6 assists in 19 regular-season games for 9 points.

He had also been part of MoDo’s squad in the championship season of 1978/79. This jersey is therefore associated with a player who was at the club both during the title-winning campaign and the year that followed. The available records do not document the particular games in which this jersey was used.
jerseys.other-01:
Brendan Shinnimin stayed with Växjö Lakers for 2018/19 after helping the club win the Swedish championship in spring 2018. He recorded 17 goals and 16 assists in 47 regular-season games for 33 points.

One of his individual highlights was a hat-trick in the home win against Mora on 28 December 2018. This jersey is from the year after the championship, when the Canadian forward was in his second season with Växjö.
jerseys.other-02:
Erik Stålnacke was one of Luleå’s forwards during the club’s early years in Elitserien. In 1985/86, he recorded 12 goals and 11 assists in 36 regular-season games for 23 points.

On 23 October 1986, he scored three goals and added an assist as Luleå beat Björklöven 9–3. The collection dates the jersey to 1985–1987, associating it with these seasons. The exact year within that period remains to be established for this jersey.
jerseys.other-03:
Erik Stålnacke recorded 8 goals and 7 assists in 26 regular-season games for Skellefteå AIK in 1982/83. His 15 points amounted to just under 0.6 points per game.

The following year, he played for Luleå in Division 1 before the club reached Elitserien. This Skellefteå jersey therefore represents the period before his move between the two northern Swedish clubs. Together with his Luleå jersey, it follows two stages of the same playing career.
jerseys.other-04:
Jens Hellgren came through Luleå’s own development system and made his senior debut in 1978/79. He spent 13 seasons with the club, playing 436 games in Division 1 and Elitserien. According to the club’s own records, he scored 197 goals and added 153 assists for 350 points.

The collection dates the jersey to 1985–1987, during Luleå’s first years in the top division. Hellgren later returned to the club as a coach. His career totals therefore cover a much longer period than the years associated with this jersey.
jerseys.other-05:
Johan Åkerman helped HV71 win the Swedish championship in 2008 after defeating Linköping in the final. The defenceman recorded 9 goals and 24 assists in 45 regular-season games for 33 points. Another 16 points in 17 playoff games followed.

After the championship season, he left HV71 for Lokomotiv Yaroslavl. In his farewell interview with the club, he described winning the title as his strongest memory from his two years in Jönköping. This jersey is dated to that final season, 2007/08.
jerseys.other-06:
Johnny Forsman joined Skellefteå AIK at the age of 16 and spent fourteen seasons in the club’s senior team. He played for the club in both 1982/83 and 1983/84. In the latter season, he recorded 9 goals and 12 assists in 35 regular-season games for 21 points.

The jersey’s date is uncertain: the folder gives 1983/84, while the image filenames give 1982/83. These statistics therefore describe one of the possible season contexts without establishing which year this jersey belongs to.
jerseys.other-07:
Josef Boumedienne was announced as a Djurgården player in summer 2010. The jersey is from 2010/11, his first season with the club. The defenceman recorded 5 goals and 25 assists in 52 regular-season games for 30 points.

He also played for Djurgården in 2011/12, recording 17 points in 36 regular-season games.
jerseys.other-08:
Kristian Näkyvä recorded 2 goals and 24 assists in 52 regular-season games for Linköping in 2017/18. His 26 points placed him tenth among SHL defencemen in regular-season scoring, according to the Swedish Ice Hockey Association’s statistics.

In the playoffs, he added another 4 goals and one assist in 7 games. This was his final season at LHC during this spell. After the season, the club confirmed that the Finnish defenceman was leaving for another SHL team.
jerseys.other-09:
Lars Hurtig joined Luleå ahead of 1985/86, making his Elitserien debut that season. He recorded 11 goals and 14 assists in 36 regular-season games. The following season, he increased his output to 17 goals and 12 assists for 29 points in the same number of games.

The collection dates the jersey to 1985–1987, the beginning of his long spell at Luleå. His career at the club later included the Swedish championship in 1996, well after the seasons associated with this jersey.
jerseys.other-10:
Linus Söderström was one of Skellefteå’s goaltenders during the championship season of 2025/26. The team won both the regular season and the Swedish championship. All three playoff series ended 4–1 in games, with Rögle as the opposition in the final.

The title was secured at home in Skellefteå on 2 May 2026 and was the club’s fifth Swedish championship. This is a photo-matched Swedish championship jersey.
jerseys.other-11:
Markus Ljungh joined Linköping ahead of 2020/21 after a season with Admiral Vladivostok in the KHL. In his first regular season at LHC, he immediately became the team’s leading scorer, recording 11 goals and 25 assists in 45 games for 36 points.

When announcing his arrival, the club described him as a centre who would help lead the team. The jersey is from his first season in Linköping, when he immediately took on a prominent role in the team’s attack.
jerseys.other-12:
Mattias Weinhandl led Elitserien in goals in 2007/08, scoring 35 in 54 regular-season games for Linköping. His 27 assists brought his total to 62 points. In the playoffs, he added another 7 goals and 10 assists in 16 games.

LHC reached the Swedish championship final, where HV71 won the series 4–2. Weinhandl continued his career in Russian club hockey after the season. The jersey is associated with one of his strongest years in Sweden, with 42 goals across the regular season and playoffs combined.
jerseys.other-13:
Robert Svehla was one of Malmö’s leading defencemen during the championship season of 1993/94. He recorded 14 goals and 25 assists in 37 regular-season games for 39 points, adding 5 goals and one assist in 10 playoff games.

Malmö beat MoDo in the Swedish championship final to win its second national title in three years. During Svehla’s time at the club, the team also won the European Cup in 1993. According to the collection’s dating, this jersey is from the season that ended with the Swedish championship in 1994.
jerseys.other-14:
Roger Åkerström recorded 6 goals and 2 assists in 37 regular-season games for Luleå in 2004/05. He also appeared in 4 playoff games. The jersey is associated with the later stages of his long career in the club’s defence.

Åkerström was captain for seven of his nineteen seasons as a Luleå player. The club retired his number 28 in January 2017. During that tribute, Luleå highlighted his decisive goal in the last game of the 1996 Swedish championship final.
jerseys.other-15:
Roger Åkerström recorded 6 goals and 2 assists in 38 regular-season games for Luleå in 2003/04. In the playoffs, he added another 3 points in 5 games, with one goal and two assists.

By then, he was an experienced member of the team’s defence and one of the club’s long-serving players. Åkerström had helped win the Swedish championship in 1996 and served as captain for seven seasons in total. This jersey represents the later part of his playing career.
jerseys.other-16:
Thomas “Bulan” Berglund’s Luleå jersey is from 1988/89, the season in which he made his debut for the club’s senior team.

It was the start of seventeen seasons as a Luleå player, lasting until 2004/05. During that time, he helped the club win its first Swedish championship in 1996.
jerseys.other-17:
Tony Mårtensson’s Brynäs jersey is from the 2001/02 season, his second and last at the club before moving to North America. He recorded 9 goals and 17 assists in 50 regular-season games for 26 points.

The previous season, he had recorded 15 goals and 11 assists in the same number of games. That gave him 52 points in 100 regular-season appearances for Brynäs. In summer 2002, he moved to the Anaheim organisation.
jerseys.other-18:
This jersey is from 1984/85, Ulf Isaksson’s final season with AIK’s senior team. He began the season as a Swedish champion. He had scored during the final series against Djurgården in spring 1984 as AIK claimed the title.

In 1984/85, he recorded 7 goals and 8 assists in 33 regular-season games for 15 points. It marked the end of a long spell at AIK after his return from the Los Angeles Kings, where he had played in the NHL in 1982/83.
jerseys.other-19:
Åke Lilljebjörn played for Leksand in 1993/94 alongside the younger goaltender Johan Hedberg. He appeared in 23 regular-season games, recording a save percentage of 90.4% and allowing 2.78 goals per 60 minutes.

A contemporary match programme from October 1993 confirms his place in Leksand’s squad that season. The jersey is associated with these years at the club, although no particular game in which it was used has yet been documented.
